svg:
Wind effect on Doppler – master formula with medium velocity w <line x1="100" y1="150" x2="700" y2="150" stroke="#222" stroke-width:1" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
source S (v_s)
observer O (v_o) wind w → (along line S→O positive) <line x1="300" y1="100" x2="350" y2="100" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:1.5" marker-end="url(#ah2)"/>
f' = f * [ (v ± w) ± v_o ] / [ (v ± w) ∓ v_s ] Take +w if wind blows from S to O (helps wave reach O faster). In numerator: +v_o if observer moves toward source (against wind? careful) Standard sign convention (1D, positive from source to observer): f' = f * (v + w + v_o) / (v + w - v_s) with v_o positive toward source? Let's state clearly in text: use line-of-sight projections. Simplify: effective sound speed v_eff = v ± w. Then apply usual Doppler with v_eff. Valid: uniform wind, |w|≪v, steady, no turbulence.
